# Observability for LLM Applications

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/observability-for-llm-applications)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/observability-for-llm-applications/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/observability-for-llm-applications) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-observability-for-llm-applications/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-observability-for-llm-applications/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

How to find where an LLM application's time, tokens and money went, and which step failed: GenAI conventions, traces across processes, a backend, cost, latency, failures, alerts, regressions, sampling and privacy, worked on a personal assistant's back end over MASSIVE's English utterances, with its own tools, retrieval and an MCP server.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For engineers who run an LLM feature in production and need to know why it was slow, expensive or wrong.

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.13.16
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python replay-one-message.py
```

The examples load an open model, pinned to an exact commit with every file's SHA-256 in `examples/models.toml`: [Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507/tree/cdbee75f17c01a7cc42f958dc650907174af0554). The first run downloads it from Hugging Face (about 11 MB); after that, the examples run offline.

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a hosted model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, the examples that use it run again in the new version, and every example runs again each week. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/observability-for-llm-applications/changes).
